I think this is all but certainly going be PlayStation - Virtual Reality. I'm expecting a VR+system package in the $600 range. Expensive relative to console norms, but Sony would be subsidizing a huge chunk of the cost - and it'd be, by far, the cheapest way to get into VR. Think about how much they dumped to establish blu-ray as a standard. And VR will likely completely dwarf blu-ray and all sorts of optical media in terms of impact. Getting a dominating position from the get go? Yeah, I think they're going to go for it.

That's the thing. I wouldn't expect it to be an entry level setup. The fundamental problem with the PS4 and XBone was that the companies, for the first time, did not subsidize the hardware costs. When you bought an original XBox for $300, the video card in that machine was north of $300 by itself. When you bought a PS4 for $400 you were getting about $400 of hardware. That's nice for short term profits, but people expect these things to last for 5-10 years and $400 hardware starts to look noticeably outdated after a couple of years, let alone 5-10. If they do go VR, I'd expect it to be more than just an entry level setup so it's not obsolete 3 years later.

This either is going to end up entering a cycle of not having enough exclusives to justify an upgrade so no one ends up making exclusives for it, or it's going to piss off current PS4 owners and burn the goodwill Sony garnered at the PS4's announcement. There's historical precedent for both: the n3DS (and to a lesser extent WiiU) for the former, and the Saturn being dumped for the Dreamcast for the latter. I don't see this working out well for Sony unless they can manage to add value to the Neo without ditching the PS4 completely, which historically has been next to impossible.
